Born at Leiden, Holland, to the Separatist exile Edward Southworth.
His widowed mother Alice married Governor William Bradford at Plymouth in 1623;
Constant followed in 1628. Lived at Duxbury; deputy to the General Court and treasurer of Plymouth Colony from 1659
to 1678. Died 10 March 1679. Daughter of William Collier, a London merchant who helped finance the Pilgrims and came
to Plymouth in 1633 in the Mary and Jane with his four daughters.
Married Constant Southworth of Duxbury 2 November 1637.
His will of 27 February 1679 left her the house and mill for life and made her sole executrix;
she swore to the inventory at Plymouth court 7 June 1679.
